description: Calcium is a chemical element with symbol Ca and atomic number 20, classified as a reactive alkaline earth metal that forms a dark oxide-nitride layer when exposed to air. It is the fifth most abundant element in Earth's crust and the third most abundant metal after iron and aluminium. The name comes from the Latin word calx meaning lime, which was obtained from heating limestone.
uses: Calcium compounds are widely used in many industries including foods and pharmaceuticals for calcium supplementation, in the paper industry as bleaches, as components in cement and electrical insulators, and in the manufacture of soaps. The pure metal has few applications due to its high reactivity but is sometimes used in small quantities as an alloying component in steelmaking and in calcium-lead alloys for automotive batteries. Calcium carbide, a major organocalcium compound, is produced in several million tons annually and is used in welding and as a chemical precursor.
characteristics: Calcium is a very ductile silvery metal sometimes described as pale yellow, with a melting point of 842°C and boiling point of 1494°C. It has a density of 1.526 g/cm³ at 20°C, the lowest in its group, and is harder than lead but can be cut with a knife with effort. Calcium spontaneously reacts with water to produce calcium hydroxide and hydrogen gas, and forms a mixture of calcium oxide and calcium nitride when exposed to oxygen and nitrogen in air.
